thread:
sean.sales: Hey team — running a POC with FinEdge. They use our TypeScript SDK behind a corporate proxy and are seeing intermittent 429s + socket timeouts. Blocker for closing this week. Any ideas?

maya-eng: Can you paste the client init and the exact error? 429s usually mean retry/backoff or shared IP throttling. Timeouts could be their proxy.

sean.sales: Here's what their engineer sent:
```ts
import Redwood from '@redwood-inference/sdk';
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY, timeoutMs: 8000, maxRetries: 2 });
await client.generate({ model: 'rw-gpt-1', prompt: '...' });
```
Errors: `Error: request aborted` and repeated `HTTP 429` in logs. They said increasing timeout to 30s helped once but 429s persisted.

alex-devex: Two quick checks: 1) Are they using an HTTP proxy agent (axios/tunnel) that preserves keep-alive? Corporate proxies often tear connections. 2) Which endpoint URL are they pointing to — the regional cluster vs global?

sean.sales: They put RW endpoint through the proxy host: `https://api.redwood.example.com` (default). Using node 18 fetch behind corporate Squid.

leo-sre: If they're hitting 429s only, could be NAT IP pooling on their egress. Our rate limits are per-API-key + per-IP in some edge cases. Ask them to confirm whether multiple users are NATting from same IP. If so, we can temporarily relax the IP window for the trial account while we validate.

jordan-security: Also get their security team to confirm TLS inspection is not rewriting headers. We saw malformed `connection` headers cause connection resets previously.

sam-sales: FinEdge asked about pricing impact if we open window — want clear commit if we give a temporary bump. I'm fine to authorize a short burst but need engineering signoff.

maya-eng: For the SDK, try setting explicit retry/backoff and exponential jitter. Example pattern: maxRetries=5 with backoff starting 200ms. If proxy kills long-lived connections, chunking and shorter TCP keepalive helps.

sean.sales: They tried bumping maxRetries to 5 and still saw long gaps where requests never hit our logs (so probably dropped at proxy). Attached network trace excerpt:
```
[13:02:11] CONNECT proxy.corp:3128 -> api.redwood.example.com:443 (established)
[13:02:12] TLS handshake completed
[13:02:14] POST /v1/generate -> 200 OK  (only some requests)
[13:02:14] POST /v1/generate -> 429 Too Many Requests
[13:02:16] socket hang up
```

alex-devex: If some requests never hit our logs, then yes proxy is dropping them pre-e2e. Two workarounds: 1) Recommend they whitelist our domain and avoid proxy for traffic to Redwood. 2) Use our dedicated POC endpoint (we can provision a short-lived dedicated IP) so their egress rules can be configured specifically.

leo-sre: I can provision a temporary dedicated IP and create a short-lived routing rule for the trial. Need customer name + expected TPS.

sean.sales: FinEdge expects ~2 qps average, spiky to 10 qps. Customer agrees to a 72-hour window.

jordan-security: They'll likely ask for an ACP/SEC questionnaire update. If we open a dedicated IP we should log the justification and expiration and update the security ticket. I'll draft the note.

sam-sales: Fine from sales. Do we need legal approval?

alex-devex: Not for a transient infra change. Engineering + security sign-off is enough. I'll coordinate with leo.

leo-sre: Provisioning now — giving them IP 34.214.98.12 (temp). Please tell them to whitelist that and disable proxying for api.redwood.example.com during the window.

sean.sales: Sent IP and instructions to FinEdge. They asked: will this affect their billing or throttle windows?

maya-eng: No billing change. Operationally their API key still enforces per-key quotas — the dedicated IP only avoids added NAT-IP noise. For throttling we'll keep close watch and can bump token throughput if needed.

redwood-deploy-bot: [info] Temporary route created for customer=FinEdge, ip=34.214.98.12, expires=+72h.

sean.sales: They followed instructions and confirm 0x0 429s so far. One last ask — they want a short doc snippet for their security team explaining why the proxy caused issues and how we mitigated it. Can someone paste a 2–3 line explanation?

jordan-security: "Corporate HTTP proxies may reset or drop TLS connections and rewrite headers, causing intermittent socket aborts and perceived 429s. Providing a dedicated egress IP (or whitelisting our domain) ensures requests reach Redwood directly, avoiding proxy-induced connection failures."

sean.sales: Perfect. Closing the loop with FinEdge. Thanks all :tada:

maya-eng: Nice. Please drop any follow-up if they ask for SDK code samples for proxy bypass in Node.

sean.sales: Will do.
